top_categories.workout_context: At mile 60 of 99, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
54ft/mi means long efforts at or near FTP on every climb. If your threshold cracks at minute 15, you'll walk the rest.
5,423ft of climbing means repeated surges above threshold. VO2max work is how you survive the fifth climb, not just the first.
Race-pace efforts that mimic GFNY Cali's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before July.
GFNY Cali's fast valley roads with long rolling and climbing forces constant power changes. Accelerate over rises and out of corners, settle on the open road, and repeat for 99 miles.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 99 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
At GFNY Cali, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of GFNY Cali. Train it until it feels boring.
5,423ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
The aerobic base that lets you ride fast valley roads with long rolling and climbing at tempo for 99 miles without cracking. No shortcuts.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 99 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At GFNY Cali, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.

race_overlay.heat: July in Cali, Valle del Cauca, Colombia can bring heat. Complete 3–4 heat exposure sessions in the final 2 weeks before GFNY Cali. Increase sodium intake 48 hours before race day.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for GFNY Cali’s 99 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Moderate altitude at GFNY Cali. Arrive 2–3 days early. Reduce intensity expectations by 5–10%. Hydrate aggressively.
race_overlay.terrain: Mixed terrain at GFNY Cali requires surface adaptability. Include weekly rides on fast valley roads with long rolling and climbing sectors to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, TT Threshold, and VO2max to prepare you for 99 miles of fast valley roads with long rolling and climbing sectors in Cali, Valle del Cauca, Colombia.
